source.title: Modeling from Features: a Mean-field Framework for Over-parameterized Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Cong Fang; J. Lee; Pengkun Yang; Tong Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes scaled Gradient Descent through a mean-field neural feature flow and proves a conditional global-minimum result for ResNets, but reports no benchmark classification-error experiments.
record.gate_note: No CIFAR or other benchmark training classification errors are reported. The paper's own conditional theorem about global optimality is recorded; cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves a conditional global-optimality theorem for a continuous, fully connected ResNet model. This does not test any stated version: it establishes neither CIFAR classification-error outcomes nor comparative effects of width, depth, initialization, learning rate, or batch normalization. A different method alone does not make it T2 when the question differs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors introduce a feature-based mean-field framework, prove finite-time approximation of sufficiently wide networks trained by scaled gradient descent under suitable initialization and step-size conditions, and prove conditional global optimality for ResNet neural feature flow. They assume convergence for the optimality theorem; they do not establish unconditional convergence of finite networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses scaled Gradient Descent and a continuous mean-field analysis; the stated results are conditional theoretical guarantees, not benchmark training-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The ResNet global-optimality result depends on Assumptions 5–8, convexity of the loss in its first argument, and convergence of the feature flow.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 11 proves that, under Assumptions 5–8 and convexity of the loss in its prediction argument, convergence of final hidden features in l∞(p) and output weights in l1(p) implies globally minimal empirical loss for the continuous ResNet flow at arbitrary finite depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated activation, initialization, support, approximation, and convergence assumptions, continuous ResNet neural feature flow attains globally minimal empirical loss.

record.problems: The global-optimality theorem requires strong assumptions and convergence of the flow; the paper reports no empirical benchmark classification-error results.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying outcomes on the claim's training behavior were reported. Referenced prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and effects of model size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction by one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation in plain convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply because no row tests V1–V6. Initialization constructions and nonvanishing feature variance do not establish initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth. Likewise, arbitrary-finite-depth conditional optimality does not establish the plain-versus-residual depth comparison in V3.

versions.untested_parts: No benchmark classification errors, corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, or stopping and regularization comparisons.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width comparison.
No plain-network comparison, depth sweep, or measured training-error comparison between plain and residual networks.
No initialization comparison measuring training speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability, curvature, loss-rise, or divergence experiment.
No batch-normalization comparison or measurement of training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: continuous Res-Net neural feature flow
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically analyze scaled Gradient Descent via neural feature flow; establish global optimality conditional on convergence and stated assumptions.

conditions.value: Assumptions 5–8; loss convex in the first argument
features converge in l∞(p) and output weights converge in l1(p)

rows.measure: Convergence to a globally optimal solution of the empirical learning task
rows.value: Theorem 11 states that the loss converges to the minimum empirical loss under the stated assumptions and convergence conditions.
rows.uncertainty: Theorem 11 is conditional; approximation theorems state probability 1 − δ.
rows.note: The theorem concerns the continuous mean-field dynamics and a general convex loss; it does not report classification error or establish that the minimum loss corresponds to zero classification error.
rows.check: The conditional theorem is correctly summarized, but its subject is a theoretical continuous mean-field ResNet, rather than an evaluated toy network. The architecture includes a bounded activation on residual branches. Theorem 11 assumes convergence of final hidden features and output weights; it does not prove that convergence occurs. Its empirical-loss conclusion does not establish any version's specified training behavior.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
